title: d-3: dependency-qualification
description:
## Deliverables
1. Perform the complete changed-registry dependency sweep across root, template and separate-consumer inputs: replace exact/tilde pins, bare versions and carets with >= tested floors and no upper bound, update rmcp to patched >=3.9, preserve features, adapt source/API call sites and qualify Windows/Monty under the supported toolchains — REQ-RUN-0002/0005; NFR-RUN-0007; ANC-012/037.
2. Update sc-config/sc-transport/sc-runtime READMEs alongside changed API/dependency behavior; preserve documented test-util helper and synchronous sc-config scope — REQ-RUN-0702; NFR-CFG-0002; NFR-RT-0001.

3. Own pin removal in crates/sc-command/Cargo.toml, crates/sc-runtime/Cargo.toml (normal/dev lines), template/crates/daemon/Cargo*.toml and tests/contracts/phase-c/application-control/Cargo.toml: rmcp >=3.9, utoipa >=6.0.0, utoipa-axum >=0.3.0; command sc-observability-types >=1.5.0 and schemars >=1.2.3 (the command manifest schemars pin at line29). Preserve the unpublished compile-fail fixture crates/sc-runtime/tests/fixtures/utoipa5-router/Cargo.toml with incompatible utoipa-axum ^0.2.0; it is test input, not a published SDK or template dependency. Preserve feature flags and its negative assertion — ANC-037.

## This sprint does not close
No Storage/CronStorage implementation, generated application wiring or registry release is closed here. d-5 owns shared root Cargo/version/lock/boundary edits, d-6 backend dependencies, d-9 cron dependencies; this sprint owns command manifest initially; d-10 follows and adds storage dependency/exports/docs. Qualified source is consumed by d-12; d-11 independently tests generated integration.
design:
Open registry floors and tested recommendations (ANC-037/038):

Every registry dependency requirement in published crates and templates uses >= a tested floor with no upper bound, including SDK dependencies. Convert bare-version and caret requirements as well as exact/tilde pins. Consumers may pin any versions in their own manifests or lockfiles. The release recommends its tested combination instead of restricting consumer choices (owner m6 extension; ANC-037). Preserve existing dependency features.

Rusqlite qualification and its one manifest owner are d-6; this sprint does not repeat that work.

Monty and monty-types remain optional and use >=1.4.0. The normal suite tests the selected versions on the documented toolchain. Intentional non-shipped negative fixtures retain their incompatible identity; they do not constrain consumers.


The root Cargo.toml currently declares only sc-observability-types as a workspace dependency; rmcp and other actual third-party declarations are in crate manifests. This sprint owns explicit sc-config/sc-transport/sc-runtime manifests and enumerated command/runtime compatibility source, no crates/** wildcard. d-5 owns root Cargo.toml registration; d-12 owns canonical Cargo.lock/version conversion, shared template manifests and contract versions. The contract owner applies only the agreed range edits in those shared files; d-3 owns source adaptations and normal tests, not concurrent shared-manifest mutation. Local tests may use disposable locks; d-12 regenerates/commits the final canonical lock after source owners close. No hard dependency on d-5 is inferred from release baseline.
sc-command lib.rs/README/storage.rs/tests/storage_combinators.rs (d-10) are explicit exclusions from this owner's enumerated source/test paths. Current API adaptation files are enumerated, not hidden behind wildcard ownership. Existing features/schema negative fixtures remain meaningful; preserve utoipa5 rejection fixtures and narrow their incompatible identities only with existing adjacent reasons. Source adaptations do not add ATM/sc-compose production dependencies.
Closure note: integration applies to this complete independent feature, even in the first wave; its actual API/toolchain interactions and executable acceptance close here, not an unimplemented contract.
Own complete sc-command and template daemon manifest rmcp changes here; no d-5 parallel edits. Workspace remains development0.2.0; only d-12 bumps final coordinated0.3.0. d-10 consumes this manifest and follows d-3 to add sc-storage later. D-5 common command traits live in sc-storage, so this sprint needs no new storage dependency to close. Native check uses cargo tree; umbrella SQLx mixed feature conflict is handled by d-7/8 direct crates and fully integrated in d-11.
Pin-edit counterpart: approved pre-dispatch ADR amendments already govern both tracks; d-5 owns matching dependency conversions in template/Cargo.toml/workspace.template.toml; d-3 owns the command/runtime/phase-c/daemon pin lines and normal tests above, and does not re-edit d-5 lines. d-9 owns sc-cron-commands manifest pins; d-12 owns cron-consumer schema manifest pins. Existing staged manifest handoffs stay unchanged; no file moves or new dependency.

dependencies.design:
## Approved design and authority
User direction01M76WCWNFNN7TCQ5WJ7CGQP4X supersedes withdrawn optional cron backend feature. No backend->sc-cron dependency or consumer-specific schema/SQL. sc-storage is std-only/no sc-*; public backends implement generic Storage<T> and atomic default per engine. sc-cron owns domain policy and maps CronRow through generic metadata; template schema owns WidgetRow/key/CRUD extension. Eight released packages: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite and existing sc-config/sc-transport/sc-command/sc-runtime/sc-cron/sc-cron-commands, coordinated0.3.0.
ANC-033: atomic transaction producer creates a fresh owned Send+'static future per attempt. Spec has only name and mode (read-only/read-write). Observability wrapper records name/queue wait/run time/row operations/outcome. SQLite submits one message/savepoint; Postgres/MySQL begin/commit and engine serialization retry. Read-only may use reader pool. SQLite awaits must be tx-handle operations; transaction-safe callees checked by external analyzer; actual Pending rolls back with typed error. Exact handle/row/multi-type shape is d-5 prototype decision; multi-type transactions unbuilt, not forbidden. Existing atm-core carries typed operations, not these futures: no claim this mechanism was copied/prototyped. ANC-034 forbids consumer table code in backends. ANC-035 public storage functions changed here return typed Results and never panic; ANC-036 writer panic fails all pending callers, no hang.

## Authoritative SQLite writer constraints
ANC-021..028 and ADR-RUN-0011: app/cron share default app DB/handle; one async channel, writer thread owns the only write connection; queued writes commit together and success replies follow commit. No caller blocking/spawn_blocking bridge, no SQLx SQLite driver. Only writer-owned runtime may Runtime::block_on; no Handle/futures variant exception. Reader blocking_recv needs no runtime. Domain guarantees (active-name/row-limit/per-row FENCED/atomic multi-row) are implemented once in sc-cron and tested through shared conformance. Migration is sc-cron/application code, not backend-specific CronRow SQL.

## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.

## Manifest ownership and closure builds
Every concurrently runnable pair has disjoint full-file fences. Only declared staged handoffs across a must_follow path share files: d-3 command manifest to d-10, d-5 additive contract/manifest/legacyAPI edits to d-6/7/8/9, then d-12 final shared version changes after source owners. Root Cargo adds sc-storage and one rusqlite >=0.41 requirement with no upper bound in d-5; current legacy cron and writer inherit it. D-5 absorbs legacy SQLite API drift and runs existing tests. Root Cargo.toml follows the declared d-5 -> d-6 -> d-12 handoff: d-6 owns rusqlite range qualification and d-12 changes only sc-* release versions; d-9 removes legacy DB dependency after generic conformance, not after a sibling's unobservable event. No parallel same-file edits. Single canonical root Cargo.lock owner=d-12, regenerated before exact release archives after all public source owners close. Earlier sprints build/test with regenerated temporary worktree locks; each cargo build --workspace passes at its own closure. D-12 owns0.2.0->0.3.0 and sibling literal->workspace inheritance, e.g. sc-runtime command/transport at21/22/39, sc-cron command at29/55, sc-cron-commands command/cron at19/20/27 in current source. No incompatible0.2.x public removal is uploaded.

## Requirement criterion ownership
REQ-RUN-0002/source-ranges and source compatibility = d-3; REQ-RUN-0002/published-consumers, archive/release and upstream-subject = d-12. REQ-CRON-0004/generated-app DB behavior = d-11; released beads-cache subject = d-12, relying on its actual upstream tests without duplicating generated-app criteria. Boundary sprints only implementation conformance, no feature closure. REQ-RUN-0326 no-DB+cron rejection = d-11, not Postgres/MySQL layer requirements. d-4 independent tooling integration owns CLI floor/archive/executable/report end-to-end feature, not storage integration. d-3 independent dependency feature integration owns actual crate APIs/features/CI; both integration closures have explicit vertical rationale despite first-wave location.

## Ratification and external gates
D-5 proposed template create/delete-with-generated-id extension over atomic storage preserves current DTO behavior; PENDING USER RATIFICATION. D-5 closes ADR0020 Open1-4 with dated text; pending owner ratification gates d-5 closure; layers consume its closed, frozen contract. Item5 synchronization stays deferred; ADR0021 transform and extra-path amendments record actual decision, no invented permission design. No publication before ratification. External no-panic rule randlee/sc-lint#931 and second await/transaction-safe analyzer rule (not yet requested; lead owns external request) are real dependencies, not fabricated sprint implementations. Runtime Pending detection is additional, never a substitute for build-time analysis. Mark missing external rules/approvals as blockers, never waive them in a green claim.

## Release order and gating
D-12 has a hard d-11 prerequisite in the phase index and live dev-to-sanity blockers; its branch targets the completed d-11 branch. It starts after that sanity and callable handoff. Before first crates.io upload, also require that checker passing on the exact archives, current owner ratification and actual required external rules. D-12 then final0.3.0 manifest/lock conversion, exact archive rehearsal, publish actual dependency DAG sc-storage first, and fresh registry-only proofs. All8 packages match source API/README; failure/yank/retry policy stays explicit in d-12. Upstream closure=beads-cache PR open with CI green at recorded SHA against published0.3.0; merge not required, maintainer=user/randlee. No response leaves d-12 open, no source/fork substitute. Final gate checks both integration outcomes; the d-11 prerequisite creates the explicit fourth sprint wave.

## Dependency security/qualification facts
The owner-directed workspace rusqlite requirement is >=0.41 without an upper bound, so consumers can select later security fixes. The normal test suite checks the selected versions. Rusqlite0.41 selects patchedlibsqlite3-sys>=0.39. Current SQLx umbrella features used by PostgreSQL/MySQL introduce SQLite resolution and conflict even with SQLite feature off. Direct sqlx-core/driver/macros resolve+check (lead probe), while real query!/offline/sqlx-cli remain unverified until d-7/8. Layer mixed probes compile actual driver + generic writer; d-11 qualifies complete generated mixed layouts after siblings. Always inspect selected cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys / -i sqlx-sqlite; Cargo.lock lists optional SQLx SQLite even when not selected and is not identity proof. No downgrade to vulnerable rusqlite. All published/template registry requirements have open tested floors (ANC-037).

## Stack rule
metadata.layer is planned presentation order; sole stack writer assigns actual append-only link order by completion. pr_target is nearest consumed artifact lower bound, actual base it or descendant. No false serialization on parallel sibling's ordinal. Branch/worktree slug agrees. No implementation dispatched before plan gates.

## Lead-validated evidence (history, not delivered proof)
# run-lead validated facts (2026-11-11, plan/phase-d @ a6cc949; crates.io + rustsec advisory-db main)
1. crates.io: rusqlite 0.42.0 (published 2026-11-11T06:47Z) -> libsqlite3-sys ^0.40.0; rusqlite 0.41.0 -> ^0.39.0; libsqlite3-sys max 0.40.0. sqlx/sqlx-sqlite max 0.9.0; sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0 -> libsqlite3-sys >=0.30.1,<0.38.0. rmcp max 3.9.0.
2. RUSTSEC-2026-0459 (libsqlite3-sys, CVE-2026-119375, local WAL uninit-memory read): patched >=0.39.0; affects bundled builds 0.6.0-0.38.2. RUSTSEC-2026-0462 (rmcp, DoS): patched >=3.9.0.
3. Published sc crates at 0.2.0: sc-command, sc-config, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands, sc-runtime, sc-transport (six). sc-runtime-db-sqlite is `publish = false` -> option B must add it as a 7th published crate (or move the writer into a published crate).
4. Current pins: sc-cron rusqlite "0.39" bundled+hooks; sc-runtime-db-sqlite rusqlite "0.39" bundled; sc-command/sc-runtime rmcp "~3.8".
5. Template: store-sqlite uses sqlx 0.9 features [runtime-tokio, sqlite, macros, migrate, sqlx-toml] => bundled libsqlite3-sys <0.38 => EVERY generated SQLite app is exposed to RUSTSEC-2026-0459, with or without cron, and cannot be fixed while store-sqlite stays on sqlx 0.9. Cron opens SqliteScheduleStore at a separate path (template/config/cron.schema.json:13, crates/daemon/src/composition.rs:90, cron.rs:190).
Consequence for option A: Phase D 0.2.1 fixes the advisory for sc-cron/writer consumers (beads-cache) but generated SQLite template apps keep the vulnerable SQLite. Plan text must say so plainly; do not claim the advisory closed for generated apps.

## rusqlite + sqlx 0.9 resolution (run-lead, 2026-11-12, cargo 1.96.1, `cargo generate-lockfile` in throwaway crates)
- rusqlite 0.41 (bundled) + `sqlx 0.9 {runtime-tokio, postgres}` RESOLVES (libsqlite3-sys 0.39.1; sqlx-sqlite absent). Same for rusqlite 0.42 (0.40.0).
- Adding ANY of the sqlx umbrella features `macros`, `migrate`, `json`, `chrono`, `uuid`, `sqlx-toml` -> CONFLICT: `links = "sqlite3"`; sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0 (libsqlite3-sys >=0.30.1,<0.38) enters resolution even with the `sqlite` feature off. `derive` and `tls-rustls` resolve.
- The template's CURRENT store-postgres sqlx features {runtime-tokio, postgres, macros, migrate, sqlx-toml} and store-mysql {runtime-tokio, mysql, mysql-rsa, tls-rustls-ring-webpki, macros, migrate, sqlx-toml} CONFLICT with rusqlite 0.41 and 0.42. => sqlite-postgres / sqlite-mysql layouts do not resolve as-is.
- Workaround that resolves AND `cargo check` passes: drop the `sqlx` umbrella; depend on sqlx-core + sqlx-postgres (or sqlx-mysql) {json,chrono,uuid,migrate} + sqlx-macros {postgres,migrate,derive,macros,_rt-tokio} directly. `cargo tree -i sqlx-sqlite`: no match. Not yet verified: query! macros against a live DB, sqlx-toml offline mode, sqlx-cli migrations.
- Pinning rusqlite <=0.39 (libsqlite3-sys 0.37) resolves with the umbrella but is below the RUSTSEC-2026-0459 fix (>=0.39). Not acceptable.
- Single-SQLite-library check must use `cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys` / `-i sqlx-sqlite`, not Cargo.lock (sqlx#3211).

Test-support ownership: d-5 generic tests/support/storage contains no CronRow or cron policy; d-9 owns the one ported tests/support/cron-storage suite/double consumed by d-11 actual providers. Both external static rules must exist and pass before d-5, d-6, d-9 and d-11 close on their changed storage code; d-12 rechecks before upload. The transaction-body analyzer request is not yet filed: run-lead owns obtaining owner approval to file, then filing and tracking it with the external sc-lint maintainer. Until delivery and passing checks, these four sprints cannot close and dependent waves cannot finish; the four-wave graph is precedence, not a delivery-date promise.
## Open registry floors and tested recommendations
Owner decision 01M77BRRDR7N4YT7HAEC9570PX: all published-crate and template registry requirements use >= tested floors with no upper bound (ANC-037), not just rusqlite. Consumers may pin their own manifests/lockfiles. d-3 owns source conversion and normal tests; each backend/command owner converts its fenced manifests. d-11 owns remaining template manifests and generation of a recommended latest-tested Cargo.lock plus matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038); d-12 refreshes template/.sc-runtime/** after final0.3.0 conversion and registry availability. This is a staged d-11 -> d-12 handoff on the existing edge; the hook remains d-11-owned. The canonical repository Cargo.lock remains d-12-owned. Recommendation snapshots are consumer product inputs, not new approval certificates or a new upgrade-tool project.
